key_insight: Augmenting a Vision–Language Model with explicit object detections (bounding boxes and instance counts) grounds its visual inputs and substantially reduces counting hallucinations, achieving more accurate and reliable counts with minimal extra compute.
problem_solved: VLMs often hallucinate when asked to count objects in an image—producing incorrect or inconsistent counts—even in advanced reasoning-capable models; GroundCount addresses this by providing explicit spatial grounding for accurate instance-level counting.
method: Run a lightweight CNN-based object detector (e.g., YOLO) to produce bounding boxes, class labels, and instance counts.
Fuse detection outputs into the VLM’s input (grounding tokens, spatial prompts, or masked visual features) so the language model can reason over explicit object instances.
Aggregate/deduplicate detections and let the VLM use grounded evidence to answer counting queries, preserving reasoning while preventing hallucinated counts.
impact: Provides a practical, low-overhead way to make multimodal systems more trustworthy for counting tasks (useful in VQA, robotics, inventory, and accessibility), while keeping the VLM’s reasoning strengths intact.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Image → Object Detector (bounding boxes) → Grounding module → VLM → Count answer

paper_title: GroundCount: Grounding Vision-Language Models with Object Detection for Mitigating Counting Hallucinations
paper_authors: Boyuan Chen, Minghao Shao, Siddharth Garg, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique
